itens.titulo: Google Disrupts 1.3 Million-Device Android Botnet, Says TV Box Maker Sold Criminal Access
itens.resumo: A botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, lost control of its servers in late October in a takedown led by Google. Google says it is highly confident that device maker Videostrong intentionally put a backdoor in the boxes and sold access to criminals. They used the boxes for ad fraud and to pass other people's internet traffic through owners' home

itens.titulo: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
itens.resumo: Two critical flaws in Langflow could let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code, IBM said last week. Langflow is an open-source tool for building AI agents and workflows, and its vulnerability reports go to IBM. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 has the flaws, and the only fix is version 1.13.0. Neither flaw is in CISA's Known

itens.titulo: BTCPay Server warns of hot wallet crypto thefts on outdated instances
itens.resumo: The maintainer of BTCPay Server, an open-source cryptocurrency payment processor, has urged users to install the latest version as hackers have been draining "hot wallets" on instances running older versions. [...]

itens.titulo: Your Mobile Carrier Stores Your Call Logs for Years
itens.resumo: Mobile carriers can retain years of call and text metadata, exposing sensitive details about customers' relationships, locations, and daily routines if breached. Cape examines the privacy risks of long-term telecom data retention and how its mobile service reduces exposure by automatically deleting call records. [...]
